overrides.reason: Assumption. The measured age mix counts only people with a birth date, and 17.9% of measured people have none (people.pctNoBirthDate), but every sample person has one (decision 156). These are the measured shares restated as shares of all people, assuming the people with no birth date are adults spread like the adults who have one: each child band is the measured share times 0.821, and each adult band the measured share times 1.115. Every band keeps its measured ratio to the others in its group, so the generator, which reads these shares as weights, draws almost exactly the same ages as before.
Design choice. Small group attendance sits between the measured rate and a livelier demo church (docs/small-groups.md).
Design choice. Small groups have about 12 members (decision 33).
Design choice. Each small group has one leader, about 1 in 12 members (decision 33).

Design choice. Notes show what good use looks like, not the thin use most churches have today, so who gets notes, how many, and how often features are used are set above the measured rates (decision 78). The measured shape is kept for timing, authors, and who notes are about.

Design choice. The measured data records no unsubscribes on recipient rows and too few bounces to shape, so these are designed (decision 131). Each person reads at their own rate by connection status, set so the sample church lands near the measured share of delivered emails opened. Unsubscribes are per 1,000 recipients of each kind of send: a newsletter, another list, and a church-wide send to someone on no list. A few active emails bounce during the window, and the rest of the measured inactive share was inactive before it (pctEmailsInactiveBeforeWindow). Sends with one link get all their clicks on it, so sends with more links give their first link a little less than the measured average. Replies to mass texts and generated conversations are designed too: the measured replies were never linked to their texts, and volume is designed (decision 91). Conversations land mostly on staff members' personal numbers, as measured, and a text with no staff answer after it is often left unread.

Design choice. Church-wide texts reach the involved adults who chose text as their preference, and students hear from the student line every week, so a little more of the church gets a mass text in a month than at the measured church (95% got none). Only the share with none is graded, because the rest shifts with the month.

Design choice. A campus newsletter holds every involved adult with an active email plus a third of the others (decisions 133 and 138), so about half of active adults get mass email in a month, where the measured church reached about one in six. The other buckets shift with the month a load is graded in, because church-wide sends cluster around Easter, the fall launch, and Christmas, so only the share with none is graded.
